summary: The core is a raster-driven pixel pipeline. A single H/V counter pair in video_gen sets the sprite/tile fetch phases, CPU access slots, sprite line-buffer writes and per-pixel serialization. This is nothing like MAME's split into a tilemap callback plus a draw_sprites loop over a frame bitmap. The protection PAL, the interrupt latch and the speech-ROM bit selection are modeled as clocked board logic rather than MAME's device abstractions (fusemap simulator, tmsprom device). The only things shared with MAME are memory-map and bit-field facts any correct implementation needs, plus the fusemap data the PAL logic was worked out from.

findings.note: addr_state = hcnt(2:0)&enable_clk, is_sprite = not hcnt(8), sprite = hcnt(6:4), tile = hcnt(7:3)/vcnt(7:3). Every fetch is timed by bits of the horizontal and vertical counters, with an hcnt range of 128..511 and vcnt of 248..511, like a PROM/counter-timed board.

A 16-slot cycle interleaves sprite X/Y/code/color reads, tile code/color reads, two graphics-ROM plane reads and CPU slots. Each fetch's data is latched in a fixed slot, then the tile/sprite shift data is reloaded at slot 1111. This is a scan-time fetch pipeline, not a batch render.

Sprites are fetched during the hcnt<256 half of each line and written into a 256x6 line RAM through an address counter loaded from x_sprite. On readout, the RAM is read and cleared pixel by pixel. MAME's draw_sprites instead loops offs=0x1c..0 over a frame bitmap with transpen.

findings.signal: per-line sprite Y match by adder
findings.note: Sprite visibility comes from an adder, y_line + y_sprite + 1, checking that the top nibble is 1111. The low bits are XORed with the flip bits to form the ROM row address (lines 313-315), as adder/XOR hardware would. MAME computes sy = 256 - y - 16 and passes flip flags to gfx->transpen.

findings.signal: color mux into palette PROM per pixel
findings.note: Each pixel is the 4-bit color concatenated with 2 plane bits. A nonzero line-buffer value overrides the background via a select, and the 6-bit result directly addresses the color PROM, whose raw 3-3-2 output goes to the DAC. There is no resnet/palette-device abstraction.

findings.signal: interrupt as latch set by raster, cleared by mainlatch bit
findings.note: cpu_int_n is a flip-flop set when y_tile=11100 and y_pixel=000, and asynchronously held clear by the latched D0 written at A000. This is a hardware latch, not MAME's screen_vblank callback gated by m_irq_mask.

The PAL is a registered 6-bit down counter clocked by an external clock (vsync stands in for the RC oscillator), reduced from the equations. MAME instead runs a generic, unclocked 64x32 fusemap AND/OR simulator on every read and drives its inputs from ls259 writes. The structure differs from MAME, though the equations were derived from MAME's fusemap data.

findings.signal: speech select latch and ROM bit mux
findings.note: The six addressable latch bits written at A800 pick one of two speech ROMs and a bit position, and an edge on bit 3 starts the LPC synthesizer. This is modeled as latches and a mux clocked from a divided 1 MHz clock, not MAME's tmsprom device with its pdc/ctl bit configuration.
The 9000/9800 RAM, A000 PAL read, B000 DSW, and colorram bits 4/5 as bank/code extension match MAME. Any correct core must share these.

findings.signal: sprite visibility rule x>0 and y>0
findings.note: The keep_sprite condition matches MAME's `if (colorram[offs+2] && colorram[offs+3])`. This is plausibly real hardware behavior that both sides model, so it is weak evidence either way.
These are generic chip models and are ignored under the rubric.
